summary: Silence and stillness. In Buddhist Chinese 寂滅, stilled and extinguished, names nirvāṇa.
placement: Chosen by farthest-point sampling on the integrated Burke–Shaw trajectory, so the eight stars spread across its projected shape. 遠 takes the point farthest from the system’s centre, 孤 the most isolated of the rest, and 寂 the point nearest the centre. A design choice, not a claim.

oc.note: Placeholder, NOT an Old Chinese reconstruction. Consult Baxter–Sagart 2014 before entering a form.

satellites.title: Stillness Is Joy
satellites.evidence: The Nirvana Sutra’s half-verses: 諸行無常，是生滅法 … 生滅滅已，寂滅為樂 — all conditioned things are impermanent, they arise and pass away; when arising and passing have passed, stillness is joy. A young ascetic offers his body to a rākṣasa to hear the second half.

checked.note: 宣過去佛所說半偈：諸行無常，是生滅法…羅剎即說：生滅滅已，寂滅為樂

satellites.title: Silent, Empty, Standing Alone
satellites.evidence: Daodejing 25: 有物混成，先天地生。寂兮寥兮，獨立不改，周行而不殆 … 吾不知其名，字之曰道 — “something formed from the undivided, born before heaven and earth: silent, empty, standing alone and unchanging, going round without wearing out … I do not know its name; I style it the Way.”
